$comment: Base style-rule pack for the korean-docs tools: Korean copy rules that FIND where a
sentence needs a human. They never rewrite one.
`replace` is the suggested wording, not an instruction the script carries out: a rule
knows where a word sits, never what it means there. Two rules that each match correctly
left one sentence reading 라이선스 수량 라이선스 하나가, and 부르다 — "to call" a function and
"to invite" a person — turned 운영자를 부른다 into 운영자를 호출한다. Neither is a regex mistake.
Every rule carries `hit` (must match) and `miss` (must NOT match) examples, and
`l10n.mjs rules --test` runs them. A bare term like 텀 also lives inside 커스텀 · 시스템 ·
아이템, so a rule without a `miss` proving the near-misses it must ignore only produces
noise a reader learns to skip. A rule without examples does not belong here.
`scope`: universal — true of any Korean product copy; always applied.
saas     — true of any subscription / billing / licensing product; applied
when a project lists it in ruleScopes of its .claude/l10n.json.
Project-only rules never enter this file — they go to <project>/.claude/l10n-rules.json,
which is applied whole wherever it exists.
These rules are advisory sweeps for the finds-only loop (`l10n.mjs rules`), never
write-time gates — word-level bans belong in GLOSSARY.base.md or a project glossary.
`severity` is documentation only — the scanner never reads it. Thresholding comes from
`minPerFile` alone, so a rule labelled "warn(3+)" without minPerFile fires on the first
hit and the label lies. Write both, and keep the "(N+)" suffix equal to minPerFile.
What a minPerFile rule counts is the author repeating himself, so the recommended side of a
`금지 → 대체` contrast row is left out of the count — a catalogue prints the copy it
prescribes once per row, and counting those reported one document eleven times for saying
the very phrasing it teaches. `contrastRecommendedRanges` in scripts/lib/doc-audit.mjs holds
the four conditions that make a row recognisable, and a contrast written as flowing prose
meets none of them and is still counted.
Two rules must not share a `find` literal: each matching rule reports independently, so a
shared pattern prints the same sentence twice and a reader learns to skip the pair.
`find` entries are regular expressions. Prefer a two-or-three word phrase over a
bare word: phrases are unambiguous, single short words rarely are.
A verb rule covers the conjugation family, never one ending. Korean negation and the
connectives attach AFTER the stem, so a pattern that stops at an adnominal ending is
blind to the negative of the very habit it describes — 에 딸린 caught while
에 딸리지 않은 walked past. Write the stem plus the syllables the contraction changes
(딸[리린립려릴렸]), not a list of endings; where a form has to be excluded, exclude it
with a lookahead and say why (손대(?!지), 기대지(?! 마[세시라십])) rather than by
omitting it, because an omission reads as an oversight and gets "fixed" by widening.
Prove every branch: a hit example per added form, and a miss example for the sense that
shares the syllables (체력이 딸리지 않도록 · 난간에 기대지 마세요 · 반품지 주소).
Adding a form usually means `references/lens.txt` needs it too — `rules --test` fails a
universal rule whose hit examples the lens matches only some of. Where the missing form
is an everyday word the lens cannot afford (가지 as in 세 가지), set `lens: false` with
a `lensReason` instead of flooding the reading list.

rules.reason: The register of an official notice. Screen guidance is uniformly 「~하세요」
A double passive

A literal English `stand`. What appears on a screen 「표시된다」. **Compounds of 서다 mean something else and are excluded** — 앞서다·넘어서다·나서다·맞서다·들어서다·물러서다·마주서다·가로서다·앞장서다 speak of order and opposition, not placement. Rewriting 「평소 수신 거부보다 앞섭니다」 as 「표시됩니다」 loses the meaning. The prefixed stems are excluded with a lookbehind that also allows a space between them — letting the spaced form through would block only half the family
A literal English `stand`/`put`. Placing something on a screen is 「둔다·배치한다·표시한다」. 「계획을 세운다」 is legitimate, so the pattern is narrowed to phrases whose object is a screen element

A literal English `the screen says/tells`. A screen, a table, a badge, a card, a list 「알린다·표시한다·설명한다」. 「화면의 몫이다」·「화면이 답한다」·「화면이 밝힌다」·「목록이 보여 준다」·「카드가 기억한다」 are the same personification — rewrite with what is actually displayed, or the feature provided, as the subject
hit: 미리 보이는 일이 이 화면의 몫입니다

rules.reason: A literal English `reach`. Delivering a notification, sending to a server, connecting a system, applying a policy, or reaching a screen written as 「닿다」 loses the actual action — write 수신하지 못했다 · 전송이 완료된 뒤 · 연결할 수 없다 · 적용되지 않는다 · 접근할 수 없다. Make 「길」 concrete along with it (알림을 보내는 길 → 알림 채널). Physical contact is legitimate, so the pattern is narrowed to phrases, and a figure reaching a limit is 「한도에 도달한다」. **A figure reaching a limit is a family, not one word** — writing only 「상한에 닿는」 lets the negative (상한에 닿지 않는다) and the other limit nouns (한도 · 임계 · 최댓값) all escape. Anchoring 「에 닿」 on the stem after a limit noun catches every conjugation. **「바닥」 and 「천장」 are left out** — a foot really touches the floor and a hand really touches the ceiling, and letters do not separate those, so the reading lens takes them.
hit: 네 개의 약속이 아무 데도 닿지 않는다
서버에 닿은 뒤 도달 시각이 기록된다
수집 데이터가 교체 판단을 거쳐 준공 · 청구에 닿고 운영자가 근거를 확인한다
miss: 두 껍데기가 맞닿는 자리는 테두리가 구분한다

rules.reason: A literal English `cap`/`impose`. A limit is 「적용한다·제한한다」 — 「건다」 is office slang too. It is the same verb as putting a hat on someone, so the pattern is narrowed to phrases whose object is a limit
「견주다」 is literary. Screen text and manuals use 「비교하다」. The conjugation changes the syllable block, so the whole stem is matched — enumerating forms such as 「과 견주면」 lets 「견줍니다·견줄·견주는·견주어」 all escape

A literal English `run`. Software does not 「돈다」. Neither the particle nor the subject is enumerated — 「프로필로 돕니다」 is caught by its particle, but 「제품은 계속 돕니다」 escapes because an adverb sits between, and 「요청마다 도는」 has yet another particle. Requiring one preceding space catches all three. The space is needed because the 는 of 정도는 · 속도는 · 빈도는 is attached to a noun. **Parts that really rotate are excluded** — a fan, a motor, a disk, a wheel, a propeller really do turn, and a product that reads hardware writes those sentences. The subject stands there in letters, so a lookbehind separates them
hit: 컨테이너는 자기가 도는 기계를 알지 못합니다
miss: 정도는 충분하고 속도는 빠르며 빈도는 낮다

rules.reason: A literal English `lives` — an inanimate thing living somewhere. Where something is is 「있다·둔다·정의된다」. Enumerating objects catches only 「사는 값」 while 「사는 자리·파일·곳」 leak, so it is matched as a family, and a person really living somewhere is legitimate, so a following person noun is excluded with a lookbehind. 「~를 사는」 (buying) has a different particle and is never caught. **The space between the particle and the verb is required** — with `\s*` instead, 「대표이사는」 reads as 「이 + 사는」 and is caught.
A literal English `freeze`

A literal English `ceiling`. A quantity limit is 「상한」. It is the same word as a building's ceiling, so it is always narrowed to a phrase. 「천장을 씌우다」 is caught by this rule alone — splitting it with cap-for-impose would report one sentence twice
A literal English `hit the wall`

A literal English `embed`/`carry`. **The adnominal and negative forms are matched from the stem too** — writing only the final form 「품는다」 lets 「그 값을 품는 배포」 and 「어느 것도 품지 않는다」 escape. It overlaps with a word-final 「품」 (제품 · 부품 · 반품지), so it does not fire when the preceding character is Hangul. **The past 「품었」 and the adnominal 「품을」 are not caught** — the legitimate sense of a person holding something in mind (「의문을 품었다」) occupies that slot

A literal English `hold` — an inanimate thing holding a value, a state, or a version in its hand. It is the same verb as a person picking something up, and it overlaps in letters with the conjugations of 「듣다」 (강의를 들었다 · 의견을 들어야) and with 「예를 들다」 (사례를 들지만). **So it is not built by excluding physical nouns** — the list of words to exclude grows with every product, and a tablet, a question, a measure, and an example leaked in turn. What an inanimate thing holds is only 값 · 상태 · 버전 · 토큰 · 계약 · 권한 · 설정 · 이력 · 키, so **it fires only when the object is one of those words.** Add a new word to the list when it joins the family. **A form with the object elided is beyond this rule** — 「스냅샷은 만든 순서로 들고 있으므로」 has an inanimate subject and no object, so there are no letters left to look at, and enumerating subjects is the same construction that failed while enumerating objects. That half is taken by the reading lens's `들고[ ,)]`.
hit: 보드 설정이 킷 버전을 들고, 스킬이

rules.reason: An inanimate thing leading a procedure — personification. A rule, a record, a setting, a document cannot lead: a person acts on it, or things proceed according to it. A person or an organization leading a team, a meeting, or an investigation is legitimate, so those objects are excluded with a lookbehind.

Calling a role, an organization, a feature, or a screen a 「자리」. Use 「자리」 only for a real place, a seat, or the layout position of a screen element; elsewhere name what it holds — 사람이 소속되는 자리 → 소속 조직, 검토자 자리가 비어 있습니다 → 필수 역할인 검토자가 지정되지 않았습니다, 바깥 시스템과 잇는 자리 → 외부 시스템 연동 설정. Rendering `seat` as 「자리」 is the same. A statutory position or a formal role is not unfolded into 「자리」 but keeps its own term. Catching 「자리가 비어」 wholesale would also catch a blank in a form and an empty cell on a timeline, so it fires only when a role name precedes it. A role where a person really has to be standing — a site watcher, a guard — is left out, because 「자리를 비운다」 is the precise term for that; only roles about appointment and designation are matched. A bold lead-in in a design note compresses into this metaphor especially — 「권한과 책임이 겹치는 자리다」 is 「항목별로 두 담당자의 권한을 구분한다」, and 「한 게시물을 읽는 자리는 하나다」 is 「상세 정보는 하나의 패널에 표시한다」. **It surfaces last in name slots** — after every screen name is fixed, the table headers 「찾은 자리」·「어긋난 자리」, the label 「자리 이름」, and the statistics tile 「빈 자리」 remain. Split by what is meant: 위치 · 항목 · 화면 · 직책 · 미편성. **「N자리」 counts digits and is not a seat** — 「숫자 6자리로 정합니다」 was caught by 「자리로 정합」. Every form beginning with 「자리」 carries a condition excluding a preceding digit, which blocks the family. **Where a screen element sits is outside this rule, and 「빈 자리」 is also used in that sense** — the empty space on a row with no icon, a cell missing an image. This reason declared 「the layout position of a screen element」 legitimate from the start, but 「빈 자리」 alone lacked that exception and fired on correct sentences. Exclude it when a word naming a screen element precedes it; catch it when a role name does. **「자리표시자」 is the compound noun for a placeholder**, so 「읽는 자리표시자」 and 「담는 자리표시자」 are not this metaphor; every form ending in 「자리」 excludes a following 「표시자」.
miss: 아이콘이 놓이는 빈 자리를 그대로 둔다
그림이 없는 행은 빈 자리로 남는다
본문이 읽는 자리표시자마다 사용처의 인자를 요구한다

rules.reason: Calling something that has a real name by a metaphorical noun. 「함정」 is a failure that is easy to walk into, 「유령」 is an old value still present, 「출발점」 is a starting value — in all three the reader has to unpack the metaphor before knowing what it is, and the actual behaviour is lost on the way. 「알려진 함정」 is 「주의할 것」, 「이 함정을 밟았다」 is 「이것을 겪었다」, 「안전한 출발점」 is 「안전한 시작 값」, 「유령 행」 is 「지워지지 않은 행」. **A real trap, a real ghost, a real starting line stays** — those three have almost no place in software writing, and where they appear the preceding word says so.

A literal English `ladder`. Neither a set of stages nor a fallback order is called a ladder — write 「릴리스 단계」·「대체 채널 우선순위」·「자동 대체발송의 마지막 채널」. The movement metaphor hides what is automatic, where a person steps in, and what the final failure state is
A literal English `read back`

A literal English `call`. **Every conjugation is in scope** — writing only the final form lets 「재평가를 부르는지」·「경보를 부르지 않는다」 walk past. **Calling a person out loud is legitimate, so the object decides** — calling a name, a person, or a child is not caught, and only writing that something else (an API, a rule, a frame, a re-evaluation) is 「부른다」 is. Write the real action: 호출한다 · 실행한다 · 적용한다 · 요구한다 · 가리킨다
On a business screen 「돈」 is colloquial. Use 금액 · 결제 · 입금
A literal English `per`. Not 「주문마다의 시도」 but 「주문별 시도」
A literal English `stale`
An address or a value changing is 「변경」. 「옮기다」 is for movement in space only
A literal English `how far it got`
「우리」 is a first person that screen copy does not use
A colloquial contraction. A status label is written as a noun
A transliterated English `term`. Caught only when it stands alone — 커스텀 · 시스템 · 아이템 end in the same syllable
A loanword spelling error

「결재」 is an approval procedure. Only compounds in a payment context are caught — 「결재 신청·결재 위임」 are correct. **A compound that works for either is not caught** — 「결재 완료·결재 경로·결재 내역·결재 취소」 are all what an approval system actually says, and they cannot be told apart from the correct field names of an approval box. What is left are the words that only work for payment: 수단 · 금액 · 대행사 have no place in an approval procedure, and an approval is not 실패 but 반려
A literal English `launch`/`bring up`. A server or a container 「실행한다」; a screen element 「표시한다·연다」

The literary connectives 「함으로써·에 관하여·에 관한 사항」. One occurrence already reads as stiff, so every one is caught — 「분석하면 알 수 있다」 rather than 「분석함으로써 알 수 있다」, 「보안을 다룬다」 rather than 「보안에 관하여」, 「~에 필요한 것」 rather than 「~에 관한 사항」. **A sentence-opening 「따라서」 is fine once and split off from here** — the repetition is the habit, so `therefore-repeat` counts it per file. **Text inside 「」·『』 is not the author's sentence** — 「~에 관한 사항」 is the formal name statutes and public tenders give to a clause item, and writing that quotes such a document has to carry the name across character for character. The same expression outside quotation marks is caught as usual.

「따라서」 repeated paragraph after paragraph. Once is normal; past three times it is a habit and the flow of the sentences should carry it — delete it where the reader already knows this follows from the previous sentence, and lower it to 「그래서」 where it stays. **It is separated from the conjugations of the verb 「따르다」** — 「규칙을 따라서 만든다」 is legitimate, so only the start of a sentence (the start of a line, or after a full stop or a dash) is matched. **The split is by what precedes, not by a lookbehind on the word** — 「따라서」 after a particle is the verb, and only a sentence-opening 「따라서」 is the connective
hit: 값이 정해졌다. 따라서 이 값을 쓴다.
값이 정해졌다 — 따라서 이 값을 쓴다.

rules.reason: Machine-translation hedging — a confirmed fact is asserted (slop-gate ko-georeuro-boinda)
A literal English `from a date` — 「~부터」 is enough (slop-gate ko-robuteo-date)
A literal English `she` — Korean uses the name or the role (slop-gate ko-geunyeo)
「~을 위해」 purpose clauses everywhere — spread them across 「~하려면·~용」
A literal English `will` — a statement of fact is asserted in the present tense. A slot where 「것」 names a task to do, as in 「처리할 것」, is excluded
An abstract subject with an all-purpose verb — a literal English `brings`/`causes`
A literal English `in the case of` — 「은/는」 is enough, or drop it (slop-gate ko-ui-gyeongu)
A mechanical enumeration — 「첫째·둘째·셋째」 becomes a real list or is carried by the flow
「율」 follows a vowel or a ㄴ final consonant only; every other final consonant takes 「률」 (Korean orthography, article 11, appendix)

A literal English `depend on`/`rely on`. A condition is written as 「~해야 한다·유지 조건·선행 조건·추가 조건이 없다」. It overlaps in letters with the Sino-Korean 기대(期待), so the stem alone is not matched: a preceding particle is required — 「기대 주기」·「기대에 못 미친다」 would be caught by the stem alone. **Requiring the particle lets the adnominal form, which stands without one, escape** — 「기댄 것이 넷이라」 is such a case and is matched separately. 「기댄」 is only the adnominal of lean, since 期待's adnominal is 「기대한」, so that one is safe without a particle. **After the particle, the stem is matched rather than an enumeration of endings** — negatives and connectives attach after the stem, so a list of final forms cannot hold 「에 기대지 않는다」·「에 기댈」·「에 기댔던」. Restricting what follows 「기대」 to an ending is the boundary against 期待 — 「에 기대를」·「에 기대가」 are the noun and are not caught. **The negative form also carries the sense of leaning on a railing** — 「난간에 기대지 마세요」 is a safety notice, so it is excluded when 「마세요·마십시오·마라」 follows
hit: 회원 명부에만 기대면 방문자가 세어지지 않는다

rules.reason: Blurring a relation into 「딸리다」. Say which it is — application, inclusion, or membership — and write 「~에 적용되는·~에 포함된·~에 속한」. It is the same verb as 「일손이 딸린다」 (to be short of), so it fires only when the particle 「에」 precedes it. **The stem is matched rather than an enumeration of endings** — Korean negatives and connectives attach after the stem, so a list stopping at the adnominal cannot hold 「에 딸리지 않은」·「에 딸리고」·「에 딸릴」. The auxiliary-particle forms 「에는·에도·에만」 take the same shape and are matched too
hit: 이 대장에 딸리고 저 대장에는 없다

rules.reason: A literal English `carry`/`ship with`. A pack, a report, or a response does not 「싣고 온다」 a value — say whether it includes, supplies, or transmits it. It is the same verb as loading cargo, so it is narrowed to the 「싣고 오다」 shape and to phrases whose object is abstract
hit: 정책 팩이 바뀐 기준을 싣고 왔습니다
그 결제 사실을 실어 나를 뿐입니다

rules.reason: Covering the scope of an impact with 「통째로」. Write what changes and what stays — 「해당 시간대의 출입 기록이 누락됩니다」 rather than 「기록이 통째로 빕니다」. Handling one physical object whole is legitimate, so it is narrowed by the following predicate

Covering a result with 「조용히」. Write what the user is not told — 「전송 실패를 알리지 않고 종료한다」 rather than 「조용히 실패한다」. A person doing something quietly is legitimate, so it is narrowed by the following predicate
hit: 판정이 닿지 않는 문이 조용히 남는다
보존 레코드가 조용히 비어 있게 된다

rules.reason: Explaining a mode, a permission, or a restriction as a physical direction. 「집행 모드로 변경한다」, not 「집행 모드로 올린다」. Stairs and temperatures really do go up and down, so it is narrowed to phrases whose object is a mode, a method, or a person in charge

Approval, issuance, and submission replaced by office slang verbs of movement. Even when the status value is issued/uploaded, user-facing copy uses the Korean administrative verb — 「이용 허가가 발급됩니다」 rather than 「허가가 나갑니다」, 「결재가 요청됩니다」 rather than 「결재가 올라갑니다」. **「올라오다」 hides whether it is registration, receipt, or transmission** — 「검수에서 올라온 용어」 is 「등재된 용어」, 「충돌로 올라옵니다」 is 「충돌로 등록됩니다」, and 「승인자가 올라간다」 is 「상위 결재자가 승인한다」. **The split is by subject rather than by enumerating conjugations**: with a record a person handles as the subject — 결재 · 서류 · 건 — every conjugation of 「올라오다·올라가다」 is caught, while things that really do go up and down (an elevator, stairs, a temperature) are not in that list and are not caught. Listing conjugations instead makes 「이 올라온」 miss 「이 올라옵니다」, and both are the same slang, the latter more common on screens
hit: 승인하면 이 심사를 근거로 이용 허가가 나갑니다

rules.reason: An assertion with no grounds, and an emotional verdict. Risk and priority are explained with conditions and results — 「지정된 외부 교육기관의 회차를 예약해야 합니다」 rather than 「유일한 길이다」. When there really is only one way, write the requirement directly with 「해야 합니다·할 수 없습니다」
hit: 외부 기관 일정을 잡는 것이 유일한 길이다

rules.reason: An unnamed authority propping up a claim — English `experts argue`·`industry reports`·`some critics` rendered into Korean. rules.reason: The text says where the model's knowledge ends, or admits it found no source and then fills the gap with a plausible guess. rules.reason: A rider bolted onto a plain fact to make it sound deeper — the English `-ing` tail (`symbolizing`·`reflecting`·`underscoring`) arriving as a Korean connective ending. The text answers an objection, or rejects an option, that appears nowhere else — usually a leftover from an earlier draft. Remove the defence, and if it holds a real claim state the claim: 「문서가 중요하지 않다고 말하는 것은 아닙니다. 문제는 …」 is 「문제는 …」 (ai-tells.md §5). An objection the text attributes and answers in full, and an option a reader would actually weigh, are kept — which is why only the set openers are caught, with the ending opened to 아니·아닙 because a Korean syllable block hides one inside the other, and the judgement stays with the reader

rules.reason: A literal English `close` — finishing a work unit, a stage or a register entry written as 「닫는다」. 「닫다」 is the verb for a door, a window, a file or a connection; a stage is 종료한다, a unit is 완료 판정한다, a risk entry is 종결한다, and 「자동시험으로 닫는다」 hides which of those it means. Two shapes are caught: a work noun as the object (단위 · 단계 · 분석 · 기준선 · 결함 …) and 「~(으)로 닫다」 with a means in front (시험 · 식별자 · 인수 · 증빙 · 승인 …), which is never how a door closes. 「회차를 닫는다」 and 「이슈를 닫는다」 are left to the lens: a product that gives a collection run an open/closed state and an issue tracker whose own button says 「닫기」 share the letters with the calque, and a rule cannot tell them apart. The words between the object and 「닫다」 may not carry a full stop or a tag, so a dialog closed in the next sentence is not read as the stage before it being closed.

rules.reason: A vague `absorb` / `accommodate`.
